chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
“The thief is to be pursued regarding his theft, even if his hand has been cut off, and he is not to be left to go away with the property of a Muslim man.”

key_terms.اَلسَّارِقُ: the thief; the one who committed theft
key_terms.بِسَرِقَتِهِ: for his theft; in relation to the stolen matter
key_terms.قُطِعَتْ يَدُهُ: his hand was cut off; the fixed punishment was carried out
key_terms.مُسْلِمٍ: a Muslim; here indicating the protected property owner

ai.seo_question: Does cutting off the thief’s hand end liability for the stolen property in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the legal punishment for theft does not cancel the obligation of recovering the stolen property or holding the thief accountable for it. It emphasizes the protection of a Muslim’s property rights and the continued pursuit of justice in financial wrongs.
